headline: 12 EVM+Solana+NEAR contracts catalogued across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, BNB, Polygon, Solana, and NEAR; legacy Rainbow Bridge (ERC20Locker) holds ~$23.3M; newer OmniBridge contracts identified across all chains.

findings.text: D1: Etherscan name-tag search surfaced 0x23Ddd3e3692d1861Ed57EDE224608875809e127f tagged 'Near: Rainbow Bridge'; contract name ERC20Locker; creator 0xCc7f3dFFA25147f60B59504F0F745c57af2E365B; admin set to 0xb8e11A1Ad588863379A3e523b37D8C78070C16D9; prover constructor arg 0x051AD3F020274910065Dcb421629cd2e6E5b46c4. Blockscan also shows same address on BscScan and BaseScan (de minimis balances). L2BEAT snippet notes deposits are paused and funds migrating to OmniBridge. Other per-chain explorers (arbiscan, basescan, polygonscan, bscscan for OmniBridge addresses) not individually fetched this run—recorded in unknowns.

D2: No canonical 'Deployed contracts' docs page discovered from near.org website (which is a marketing landing page with no inline address list). OmniBridge README on GitHub at github.com/Near-One/omni-bridge/blob/main/README.md serves as the de-facto deployed-contracts document and is set as deployed_contracts_doc.

D3: No audit_links provided in protocol context; no audit PDFs discovered via fetched pages. OmniBridge README references a HackenProof bug bounty but no audit report URL was surfaced. Recorded in unknowns.

D4: GitHub repo Near-One/rainbow-bridge fetched; no broadcast/run-latest.json or hardhat-deploy artifacts visible in repo root listing. OmniBridge README (Near-One/omni-bridge) contains a full Contract Addresses section listing mainnet addresses for all 7 supported chains—used as primary deployment artifact. No pinned commit SHA obtained for OmniBridge README (branch=main); recorded.

D5: Multi-chain enumeration: Ethereum (legacy ERC20Locker + OmniBridge), Arbitrum (OmniBridge 0xd025b38762B4A4E36F0Cde483b86CB13ea00D989), Base (OmniBridge 0xd025b38762B4A4E36F0Cde483b86CB13ea00D989), BNB (OmniBridge 0x073C8a225c8Cf9d3f9157F5C1a1DbE02407f5720), Polygon (OmniBridge 0xd025b38762B4A4E36F0Cde483b86CB13ea00D989), Solana (OmniBridge program dahPEoZGXfyV58JqqH85okdHmpN8U2q8owgPUXSCPxe), NEAR (omni.bridge.near, factory.bridge.near). Block-explorer pages for Arbitrum/Base/BNB/Polygon/Solana OmniBridge addresses not individually fetched this run—recorded in unknowns for next run.

D6: factory.bridge.near is a NEAR-side factory for bridged ERC-20 tokens (NEP-141 wrappers). Per rainbow-token-connector README, tokens deployed as <hex(erc20)>.factory.bridge.near. Factory enumeration not feasible via defipunkd read API (NEAR is not a supported chainId); recorded in unknowns.

D7: Role taxonomy applied: ERC20Locker=vault (lock/unlock ERC-20), admin of ERC20Locker=admin (EOA or multisig—unknown actor class), NearProver=other (proof verifier), OmniBridge EVM contracts=vault/router, NEAR omni.bridge.near=vault, factory.bridge.near=factory, Solana program=vault.

D8: All addresses in admin_addresses[] trace to fetched URLs (Etherscan page for legacy ERC20Locker, omni-bridge README for OmniBridge addresses). Admin address 0xb8e11A1Ad588863379A3e523b37D8C78070C16D9 (admin of ERC20Locker) was read from decoded constructor args on fetched Etherscan page. Actor class of this admin address is unknown (not checked for multisig/EOA this run).

rationale.verdict: Discovery run walked near.org website, Near-One/rainbow-bridge and Near-One/omni-bridge GitHub repos, and the Etherscan page for the Etherscan-tagged 'Near: Rainbow Bridge' ERC20Locker contract. 12 addresses catalogued across Ethereum (2 legacy + 1 OmniBridge), Arbitrum (1), Base (1), BNB (1), Polygon (1), NEAR (4 account-IDs, non-EVM), and Solana (1 program). Key gaps: actor class of the ERC20Locker admin address, per-chain block-explorer verification of OmniBridge addresses, and absence of any audit report.

evidence.shows: Capability probe: near.org website fetched successfully; confirms NEAR is the official protocol; links to github.com/near org; no contract addresses listed on landing page.

Official Near-One/rainbow-bridge GitHub repo; GPL-3.0 license; Rust/JS/Go/Solidity codebase; testnet config shows ethClientAddress, ethProverAddress, ethLockerAddress fields; latest release eth2-client-v0.7.1 (Apr 9 2026); repo is an OPS tool for the NEAR<>Ethereum bridge.

Etherscan name-tag 'Near: Rainbow Bridge'; contract name ERC20Locker; verified source; Solidity 0.6.12; admin constructor arg decoded as 0xb8e11A1Ad588863379A3e523b37D8C78070C16D9; prover arg 0x051AD3F020274910065Dcb421629cd2e6E5b46c4; creator 0xCc7f3dFFA25147f60B59504F0F745c57af2E365B; holds ~$23.3M in ERC-20 tokens (USDC, USDT, DAI, WBTC etc.); methods include lockToken, unlockToken, adminPause, adminTransfer; 64306 total txs; latest activity Jul 2026 (Unlock Token). L2BEAT snippet referenced deposits paused, migrating to OmniBridge.

OmniBridge README listing mainnet bridge contract addresses: Ethereum 0xe00c629aFaCCb0510995A2B95560E446A24c85B9, Arbitrum 0xd025b38762B4A4E36F0Cde483b86CB13ea00D989, Base 0xd025b38762B4A4E36F0Cde483b86CB13ea00D989, BNB 0x073C8a225c8Cf9d3f9157F5C1a1DbE02407f5720, Polygon 0xd025b38762B4A4E36F0Cde483b86CB13ea00D989, NEAR omni.bridge.near, Solana dahPEoZGXfyV58JqqH85okdHmpN8U2q8owgPUXSCPxe. Helper contracts on NEAR: vaa-prover-0_4_3.bridge.near, vaa-prover-0_4_1.bridge.near, eth-prover-0_4_1.bridge.near, omdep.near, factory.bridge.near. Bug bounty on HackenProof. Security contact via HackenProof.

protocol_metadata.about: NEAR Bridge (Rainbow Bridge / OmniBridge) is NEAR Protocol's canonical cross-chain bridge enabling asset transfers between NEAR and Ethereum, Solana, Arbitrum, Base, BNB Chain, and Polygon. Users lock ERC-20 tokens in an Ethereum ERC20Locker contract and receive NEP-141 wrapped tokens on NEAR, or use the newer OmniBridge which leverages Chain Signatures (MPC) for outbound transfers and light clients or Wormhole for inbound verification. The legacy Rainbow Bridge is based on on-chain NEAR light clients and optimistic validation; the OmniBridge replaces it with MPC-signed proofs. Deposits to the legacy Rainbow Bridge are paused as funds migrate to OmniBridge.
